_doc: The opening cinematic, played after New Game once the lead is picked (src/ui/opening.gd, docs/25). Each shot is one picture, drawn in code, with its lines of narration shown one after another. `shot` picks the picture; `time` is how long the shot holds, in seconds, shared out evenly between its lines. Click, Space or Enter moves to the next shot; Esc skips the rest. Rewrite the words freely; a new kind of picture needs code.
_doc_cast: Who appears. `sixteen` are folders in art/sixteen/ (idle/south.png), in the order they stand in the ring; `lead` stands in for the lead who falls when none was picked (Atlas, as in every run with no pick) (the lead picked is the one shown); `party` and `foe` are unit templates in units.json; the party are six of the sixteen, never the old twelve (D79). The road (carriages) and foe (a foe remembers you) shots are cut for the First Hour (D97); their drawings stay in opening.gd for when those systems come back.
_doc_ending: `ending` is the one of the sixteen whose world is seen ending in the `ending` shot, so a new player sees the hook before they live it (D99, D101); {other} in a line is their name. When they are the lead, the next of the sixteen stands in.
_doc_replay: Every life after the first plays the opening again, after the quiz and before the landing (Will, 2026-10-15), with a slight change for who is left, until only one is. It plays only the `replay` shots: the story, not the how-to-play shots the player has already seen (call AC, about 55 s). The fallen stand grey in the ring and their worlds are dark; the `ending` shot shows the lead who has just died, not `ending`. `by_left` swaps whole shots' lines by how many of the sixteen are still alive: `many` (three or more), `two` and `last`. In those lines {Left} and {left} are how many are alive (in words, capital or not), {Fallen} how many have fallen, {left_after} how many would be left after the new lead, {dead} the lead who just died and {how} how they fell (`how`). Inferred: the words.

lines: Before the worlds, there was a contest.
Sixteen were chosen for it. Half-gods, each the best there ever was at something.
A shield-bearer, a hunter, a keeper of fires, a duelist who never lost.
Sixteen of them, and each would be given a world.
Sixteen copies of one Earth were made. In the middle of every one, a Tower.
Only one of the sixteen worlds will still be there at the end.
In one of the other worlds, it is already over.
{other} fell on the Tower's stair, and that world went dark with them. It never comes back.
Then they were thrown down.
They fell for a long time, and as they fell, they forgot.
One of them is you.
You wake at the bottom of a crater of burnt ground, with your name and nothing else.
Over everything, the Tower stands. A hundred floors, and something at the top.
Every chapter you climb gives back a little of who you were.
The world will not wait for you.
Towns trade and quarrel. A gate left alone breaks open. Miss a deadline and someone dies, or someone else is paid.
You will not climb it alone. Up to six will walk with you.
Not all of them will walk back. Here, the dead stay dead.
When it comes to blades, nobody waits their turn.
Stop the world, look, and choose. Then let it run.
If you fall, your world ends with you.
You go on as one of the others, in their world, from the beginning.
Your weapon falls after you, somewhere. Your ghost waits at the fire.
A new standing quest: Ascend to heaven.
